overview.problemStatement: The core journey (browse, event page, registration, ticket) has grown features faster than a quality floor. Dialogs and menus were built per screen, so focus entry, focus return, Escape handling, and keyboard navigation differ between them; some async actions change the screen silently; decorative motion ignores the reduced-motion preference; several controls rely on colour alone; and the event page ships more JavaScript and image weight than its content needs, so it is slowest on the phones most attendees use.
overview.proposedSolution: A hardening pass with no new capability: shared accessibility primitives (focus trap, visually hidden text, live region), landmarks and skip link, one h1 per page, labelled and error-associated fields, contrast and reduced-motion fixes, and an explicit event-page performance budget (Lighthouse mobile 95+, LCP 2.5s, CLS 0.1, first-load JS 180KB gzip). Two automated gates (axe-core and Lighthouse) make the floor regressible.
overview.targetAudience: Attendees using screen readers, keyboard only, switch access, or a low-end phone on a slow network; organizers whose event page is their storefront.
assumptions: Lighthouse is measured on a mobile profile (4x CPU throttle, 1.6 Mbps) against the production build, not the dev server.
axe-core is the automated conformance tool; roughly half of WCAG issues need a documented manual checklist.
No visual redesign is in scope: contrast, focus, and target size may change; layout and brand may not.
The event page is the performance reference page; other pages must not regress.
outOfScope: New pages, new user stories, or changes to registration semantics.
A design refresh or brand work.
Admin console accessibility beyond the shared primitives.

userStories.title: Complete the journey with a keyboard
userStories.want: to browse, open an event, register, and read a ticket without a mouse
userStories.benefit: assistive input is never a dead end

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given any public page, every interactive element is reachable in visual order with Tab/Shift+Tab, and the focused element shows a visible focus ring of at least 2px at 3:1 contrast.
Given a dialog or menu, opening it moves focus inside, Tab is trapped while it is open, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the trigger; menus also respond to arrow keys.

userStories.title: Understand the page without seeing it
userStories.want: structure, labels, and status changes to be announced
userStories.benefit: I know where I am and what happened

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given any page, it exposes a main landmark, a skip-to-content link as the first focusable element, and exactly one h1; headings descend without skipping a level.
Given a form, every field has a programmatic label and its hint and error text are associated with the input and announced when validation fails.
Given an async action (register, cancel, copy ticket code, submit feedback), success and failure are announced through a live region without moving focus.

userStories.title: See and read comfortably
userStories.benefit: the interface does not depend on perfect sight or colour perception

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given any page, text meets 4.5:1 contrast (3:1 for large text), UI boundaries and focus indicators meet 3:1, and no state is conveyed by colour alone.
Given the operating system reduced-motion preference, carousel autoplay, modal transitions, and parallax are disabled while every state change remains legible.

userStories.title: Open an event page fast
userStories.want: the event page to render quickly and stop moving
userStories.benefit: I can decide and register before I lose patience

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the production build on a throttled mobile profile, the event page scores at least 95 for Lighthouse performance and accessibility, with LCP at most 2.5s, CLS at most 0.1, and total blocking time at most 200ms.
Given the event page, first-load JavaScript is at most 180KB gzip, the hero image is served through next/image with explicit dimensions and priority, and no web font swap shifts the layout.
acceptanceCriteria.withdrawnReason: Unattainable as written: Clerk UI bundles alone are about 343KB, so a 180KB first-load JavaScript budget cannot be met while @clerk/nextjs loads its UI on public pages.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the production build, first-load JavaScript is at most 700KB gzip including Clerk UI and at most 350KB excluding it, and both numbers are recorded in the performance report.

userStories.title: Keep the floor from regressing
userStories.want: automated accessibility and performance checks in the build
userStories.benefit: a future feature cannot quietly reintroduce these problems

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a pull request, an axe-core run over the five reference pages reports zero violations of the WCAG 2.1 A/AA rule set, and a Lighthouse budget run fails the build when the event page drops below its thresholds.

functionalRequirements.text: Every interactive element on public pages MUST be keyboard reachable, in an order that matches the visual order.
Focus MUST be visible on every focusable element, with a ring of at least 2px at 3:1 contrast.
Dialogs MUST move focus inside on open, trap it, close on Escape, and return focus to their trigger.
Menus MUST support arrow-key movement, Home/End, and Escape, with the active item announced.
Every page MUST expose header, nav, main, and footer landmarks plus a skip-to-content link.
Every page MUST have exactly one h1 and a heading order without skipped levels.
Form controls MUST have programmatic labels and associated hint and error text.
Async outcomes MUST be announced through a polite or assertive live region, without stealing focus.
Colour usage MUST meet the contrast thresholds and MUST NOT be the only signal for state.
Motion MUST honour prefers-reduced-motion, disabling autoplay, transitions, and parallax.
An axe-core check over the five reference pages MUST run as a gate and report zero violations.
A Lighthouse budget check MUST fail when the event page misses its performance thresholds.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: The five reference pages MUST conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, verified by axe-core plus a documented manual checklist.
The event page MUST score at least 95 for Lighthouse performance and accessibility on the defined mobile profile.
The event page's first-load JavaScript MUST stay at or below 180KB gzip.
Cumulative layout shift MUST stay at or below 0.1, including font and image loading.
The accessibility and Lighthouse checks MUST be runnable non-interactively so CI can enforce them.
The hardening MUST NOT weaken the existing CSP, security headers, or input handling, and MUST NOT introduce dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

First-load JavaScript on the reference pages MUST be at most 700KB gzip including third-party auth UI, and application code excluding Clerk MUST be at most 350KB gzip. NFR-003 is superseded by this requirement.

edgeCases.description: A dialog trigger is removed from the DOM while the dialog is open.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Focus falls back to main rather than body.
The second traps focus and closing it returns focus to the first, not to the page behind.

edgeCases.description: A screen-reader user with reduced motion opens the carousel.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Slides become manually navigable and the position counter is announced.
Skip link, headings, and content remain readable in document order.

edgeCases.description: An event title is long and contains only emoji.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The h1 and share metadata remain understandable and do not overflow.

edgeCases.description: The event page is opened on a slow connection.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The hero image reserves its box (no CLS) and text renders before images.

dependencies.name: axe-core
dependencies.notes: Automated WCAG rule evaluation in tests and CI.

dependencies.name: vitest-axe
dependencies.notes: axe integration for the existing Vitest setup.

dependencies.name: Lighthouse
dependencies.notes: Mobile performance budget for the event page.

risks.description: Accessibility work is invisible in a demo and gets deprioritised mid-feature.
risks.mitigation: Land the automated gates first so regressions fail the build.

risks.description: Lighthouse scores are noisy across machines.
risks.mitigation: Fix the profile (mobile, 4x CPU, 1.6 Mbps), measure the production build, and assert budgets rather than screenshotting a score.

risks.description: Extracting focus primitives changes every dialog at once.
risks.mitigation: Adopt the primitives screen by screen with existing tests kept green.

risks.description: Contrast fixes flatten the muted brand palette.
risks.mitigation: Adjust only failing tokens and record before/after ratios.
